FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 18 
January 1990, after the draft finalized by the Timber Stored Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 

The general requirements for wooden handles are covered by IS 620 : 1985 'Wooden tool handles, 
general requirements {fourth revision )\ A series of Indian Standards have been prepared for 
various hand tools and for use with these hand tools, a series of standards for corresponding wooden 
handles are also published. This standard deals with the requirements of wooden handles for rasps 
conforming to IS 3587: 1986 'Specification for rasps ( second revision)', engineers' files conforming 
to IS 1931 ( Part 2 ) : 1972 'Specification for engineer's files (second revision )' and engineers' 
scrapers conforming to IS 6861 : 1973 'Specification for engineers scrapers'. 

This standard was first published in 1965 covering only the wooden tool handles for engineers' files 
and subsequently revised in 1978. Since the conditions of use of engineers' scrapers, engineers' files 
and rasps are more or less identical, the stresses and forces to which their handles are likely to be 
subjected to in service/use would also be not significantly different. Therefore, in this revision the 
requirements for rasps and engineers' scrapers have also been included. The Table 1 for dimensions 
and tolerances has been modified to include requirements, for some additional sizes of rasps/files/ 
scrapers and tolerances for individual dimensions. 

In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international coordination among 
the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it the practices in 
the field in this country. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2: 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )'. The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value 
in this standard. 



IS 2895: 1990 



Indian Standard 



WOODEN HANDLES FOR RASPS, ENGINEERS' 
FILES AND ENGINEERS 5 SCRAPERS — 

SPECIFICATION 

( Second Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements of 
wooden handles for rasps confirming to IS 3587 : 
1986, engineers' files conforming to IS 1931 
( Part 2 ) : 1985 and engineers' scrapers confirm- 
ing to IS 6861 : 1973. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard. 

IS No. Title 

620 : 1985 Specification for general require- 

ments for wooden tool handles 
( third revision ) 

707 : 1976 Glossary of terms for timber 

technology and utilization 

1931 : 1972 Specification for engineers files 

(first revision) 

3587 : 1976 Specification for rasps 

6861 : 1973 Specification for engineers 

scrapers 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the defini- 
tions given in IS 707 : 1976 and IS 620 : 1985 
shall apply. 

4 MATERIALS 

4.1 The handles for rasps/engineers' files/engineers' 
scrapers shall be manufactured from any of the 
timbers specified for Class V handles in 
IS 620 : 1985. 

4.2 The blanks shall be well-seasoned ( preferably 
air-seasoned ) to a moisture content not exceeding 
15 percent and the inclination of the grain shall 
not exceed 1 in 15. They shall be free from 



centre heart ( pith ), sapwood, any kind of decay 
( rot ), checks, shakes, splits ( except hair splits ), 
borer holes, warp and any other defect except 
those permitted in the finished handles ( see 
IS 620 : 1985 ). 

4.3 Galvanised mild steel used ferrules shall be 
from 1'6 ± 0*2 mm thick sheet or from seamless 
tubes of the same thickness. 

5 MANUFACTURE 

5.1 The handles shall be manufactured to the 
shape and design as shown in Fig. 1 . 

5.1.1 It is recommended that, immediately after 
manufacture, all tool handles be dipped 
momentarily in raw linseed oil at room temper- 
ature as this treatment retards changes in moisture 
content. 

5.2 The ferrules shall be either made from seam- 
less tube or from sheet butt welded and shall be 
snugly fitted to the handles as shown in 
Fig. 1. 

6 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 
6.1 Dimensions 

The handles shall conform to the dimensions and 
tolerances given in Table 1 . 

7 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

7.1 Workmanship and finish, permissible defects, 
tests, treatment and sampling shall be as specified 
in IS 620 : 1985. 

8 MARKING 

8.1 Unless otherwise specified, each handle shall 
be legibly and idelibly marked with indication of 
the source of manufacture and the year of manu- 
facture. In addition, the size of the rasps/engineers' 
files/engineers' scrapers which the handle is re- 
quired, shall also be marked.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as. symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, are 
issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of 
the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the 
following reference: 

Doc: No. CED33(4608)
